Published online:
    August 28, 2026

Geographic focus:
    USA (primary); Europe (secondary)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [NO]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES]

Synopsis:
    Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivered a hawkish-leaning speech at Jackson Hole, signaling that the Fed may need to raise rates further if inflation does not convincingly return to the 2% target. Markets repriced aggressively: September hike probability jumped from 35.4% to 55.7%. Short-end yields surged (2Y +12.79bps to 4.36%), the dollar rallied sharply, equities sold off broadly with tech and small-caps hit hardest, gold and silver dropped, and bitcoin fell. Oil slipped on both the hawkish tone and Strait of Hormuz shipping deal rumors.

Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US market pricing?
Relevance: YES — directly covers Fed policy signaling, Treasury yield moves, equity index repricing, and FX/commodity reactions.

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 90 (strongly YES)
Probability of increase: 55.7% (September meeting, per CME FedWatch as cited in article)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 10 (marginally — holding was the prior base case before Warsh's speech, now largely displaced)
Probability of holding: 44.3% (implied residual from CME FedWatch data cited)

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (NO — cuts are not discussed or implied anywhere in the article)
Probability of decrease: 0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: +75 (Distinctly more hawkish than before — Warsh broke from prior guidance-averse posture, explicitly flagged inflation persistence, acknowledged non-restrictive financial conditions, and market pricing shifted materially toward a hike with Wells Fargo strategist flagging potential for "one rate increase, if not more" over coming months)
